THE CARDS

TWENTY-SEVEN FACES, COMPOSED FROM THE SEALED KNOT MAP
THE WAYFINDER THE MAP ROOM THE RING THE RESONANCE THE INSTRUMENT THE LANGUAGE THE ASTROLABE THE ROSETTE THE SPECTRUM THE WORKSHOP
The deck as it will be held, at the tarot trim of 70×120 mm: twenty-seven faces composed from the sealed knot map, the mandala face over its profile. The foot takes the letter table's own arrangement, with the name standing where the letter stands there: the ternary trigram in the card's metal on one flank, the family symbol on the other, the name in white between them. The card's sound waits for the cymatic; its ratio is already written in the deck's own notation, q in the corner and p in the windings. Two diagonals close the face: the card's number and its answer's number in their own metals across one, the signed number and its negation, neutral, across the other: q is the law and wears no house. Turned upside down, the corners read as the answer's corners: an inverted card announces another card, never itself reversed. The three metals are the states themselves: silver flows (MA, the blade) · gold turns (RA, the dawn) · bronze holds still (AUM, the bulk): gold and silver mirror each other, bronze mirrors itself, and the Seed alone wears white-gold. Each suit laid out as its own 3×3 ternary square. No letter appears. The key is in Lonnie's hand.
THE PRINTED DECK
Pressed from this page, never from a second drawing of it. Trim 70×120 mm, 3 mm bleed on every edge, rebuilt by bun scripts/pressCards.mjs.
THE DECK
Twenty-eight sheets, one card per page, the page box the bleed box. Twenty-seven faces and the one back they all share.
THE ILLUSTRATED GUIDE
The little book that travels with the deck, pressed at the same trim so the two are one object in a pocket.
THE BOX FACE
The lid: the trefoil alone, no word. The same emblem the volumes carry, imported rather than redrawn.
THE PRESS NOTES
What a printer needs told: rich black not flat, the ink limit, and why the stock is the metal.
The press routes themselves, should you want the sheets rather than the files: ?press lays all twenty-eight at the true trim, and ?press&card=N fills one sheet at 300 dpi. The edition line is set with &ed=, and is identical on all twenty-seven so it tells a reader nothing about the card they hold.
